title: estimate/v2 decision
description: The cost-estimate honesty schema: contract-first, ahead of spec-lane's own estimator implementation (see docs/protocols; the 'D4 estimate 正直さ schema' design note). A decision is either `predicted` (a point estimate exists, carried in top-level `predicted`) or `abstained` (it does not, and `decision.reason_codes` says why) -- there is no third 'best guess anyway' state. `reason_codes` is split into 11 BLOCKING codes and 1 ADVISORY code (`DRIFT_WARNING`): `status == "abstained"` MUST carry at least one BLOCKING code (sol architect-review must6 -- DRIFT_WARNING alone does not justify withholding a point estimate), and `status == "predicted"` MUST NOT carry any BLOCKING code (a point estimate with a due-for-abstain reason attached would be self-contradictory). Both directions are schema-structural where a plain closed set can express them and semantic (verify-fixtures.mjs) where 'at least one of these 11, and none of that other 1' needs actual set arithmetic this repo's validator subset doesn't have a keyword for.

allOf.description: sol architect-review must6: a predicted decision requires a point estimate, structurally, not just as an implication of decision.status.

sol architect-review 2nd round must B: the tagged union's other direction -- an abstained decision must not carry a predicted object at all (not merely 'may omit it'). A predicted point estimate alongside an admission that no prediction could be made is self-contradictory.

sol architect-review 2nd round must B: applicability.status=="out_of_domain" is part of the state machine, not just informational -- out-of-domain implies the decision must abstain (there is no such thing as a confident point estimate for a surface the population math says is out of domain).
sol architect-review must6: prediction_interval's "available" state is frozen in full -- every field required together, not left partially specified.

else.description: sol architect-review 2nd round must B: the other side of the tagged union -- when status=="insufficient_data", none of the "available"-only value fields may be present either (closed to only `status` in this branch), not merely optional.

allOf.description: sol architect-review 3rd round must2: prediction_interval.status=="available" forces decision.status=="predicted" -- an abstained decision has no point estimate, so an "available" confidence interval (which is an interval AROUND a point estimate) cannot coexist with it. This closes the other direction of the same tagged-union coupling `predicted` itself already has with `decision.status`.

target.description: What quantity this decision is (or would be) predicting. Required unconditionally -- even an abstained decision was abstaining from estimating a specific, named target, not from estimating in the abstract.

predicted.description: The point estimate. Required when decision.status == "predicted" (see the top-level if/then); absent when abstained -- there is no partial or placeholder point estimate for an abstained decision. p50 <= p80 is a semantic check (verify-fixtures.mjs), mirroring spec-lane's own QuantileSchema.refine.

value_status.description: estimated (a genuine model output) | lower_bound (the population/interval math could only bound it from below, e.g. too few high-cost neighbors to characterize the upper tail).

cohort.description: What this decision's comparison population is scoped to. Required in full even for an abstained decision -- several reason_codes (MODEL_GENERATION_MISMATCH, ROUTING_PROFILE_MISMATCH, TOKEN_BASIS_MISMATCH, TARGET_BASIS_UNSUPPORTED) are only meaningful if the cohort they're a mismatch against is recorded, not omitted. The cohort's identity is the tuple (model_generation, routing_policy_digest, prompt_policy_digest, token_basis, execution_profile_digest): two decisions with all five equal are claiming to have drawn from the same comparison population. `cohort_provenance` (below) is what makes that claim checkable rather than an assertion resting on three opaque hashes.

routing_policy_digest.description: Content digest of the routing policy object in effect for this cohort (e.g. this repo's own model-bindings.json-shaped role->model mapping, or an equivalent producer-side routing table) -- sha256 of that object after RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme normalization (contracts/shared/jcs.mjs's `canonicalize`, a repo-local JCS subset: recursively sorted object keys, no floats, no non-ASCII keys), formatted `sha256:<64 lowercase hex>`. Two decisions carrying the same value here are claiming their routing policy was byte-for-byte the same object post-normalization -- see `cohort_provenance.routing_policy_digest` for how that claim can actually be checked (recomputed and compared for `inline`, or merely named for `locator`/`unavailable`).

prompt_policy_digest.description: Content digest of the prompt/system-prompt policy object in effect for this cohort -- same JCS-then-sha256 construction as `routing_policy_digest` (contracts/shared/jcs.mjs), formatted `sha256:<64 lowercase hex>`. See `cohort_provenance.prompt_policy_digest` for how the referenced object can be recovered or verified.

execution_profile_digest.description: Content digest of the execution profile object in effect for this cohort (agent harness/tool-access/sandbox configuration) -- same JCS-then-sha256 construction as `routing_policy_digest` (contracts/shared/jcs.mjs), formatted `sha256:<64 lowercase hex>`. See `cohort_provenance.execution_profile_digest` for how the referenced object can be recovered or verified.

cohort_provenance.description: For each of the three digest fields above, how its referenced policy object can actually be recovered or checked -- closing the gap `additionalProperties: false` on `cohort` would otherwise leave: a digest alone has nowhere to record what it is a digest OF. Modeled on decision/v1's $defs/artifact_ref honest-reference convention (content_digest+uri, verified byte-for-byte by contracts/shared/verify-artifact-digests.mjs when the uri resolves inside this repo) but adapted for a JCS-normalized-object digest rather than a raw file digest: `inline` carries the actual pre-normalization object so contracts/shared/verify-cohort-provenance.mjs can recompute and compare it directly (no filesystem or network access needed -- this is the strongest state and can run in CI unconditionally); `locator` names where the object lives without embedding it (checkable structurally -- something is named -- but not digest-verifiable by this repo's own CI); `unavailable` is an honest admission that no resolution path exists (e.g. a policy object that lives in a private repo and cannot be shared), and MUST carry `reason`. There is deliberately no fourth 'no referent needed' value: unlike `decision/v1`'s digest_omitted_reason (where the digest itself may legitimately not exist), all three digests here are unconditionally required, so their provenance is either resolvable in one of these two ways or honestly marked as not resolvable -- never silently absent.

population.description: eligible_count MUST be <= candidate_count (a semantic check, verify-fixtures.mjs -- comparing two sibling fields isn't a plain schema constraint in this repo's validator subset).

excluded_by_reason.description: Map of reason_code (same closed set as decision.reason_codes) to excluded count. Counting rule (sol architect-review 2nd round must B, main裁定 -- EXCLUSIVE primary-reason counting): each excluded candidate is counted under exactly ONE reason_code -- the first one, in the reason_codes enum's declared order, that applies to it. A candidate is never counted twice under two different reasons. Consequently sum(excluded_by_reason values) MUST equal candidate_count - eligible_count exactly (verify-fixtures.mjs enforces this; an excluded_by_reason that sums to less than the gap is silently dropping candidates with no recorded reason, which this rule forbids). Left schema-unconstrained as to keys/values individually (this repo's minimal validator subset does not support per-value schema validation of arbitrary-keyed maps) -- sol architect-review must7 enforces per-key/value shape as semantic checks in verify-fixtures.mjs: every key must be one of the 12 reason_codes, every value a non-negative integer, and (this round) the sum must reconcile with candidate_count - eligible_count.

prediction_interval.description: Whether enough calibration history (leave-one-out error samples) exists to also emit a confidence interval around the point estimate -- orthogonal to decision.status: a `predicted` decision (a point estimate exists) can still have prediction_interval.status == "insufficient_data" (not enough LOO history yet to bound it). When status == "available", level/lower/upper/method/calibration_sample_size are ALL required together (schema if/then, sol architect-review must6 -- the "available" shape is frozen in full, not left partially specified) and lower <= upper is a semantic check (verify-fixtures.mjs). v2's own fixture set exercises both insufficient_data and a fully-shaped available example (see fixtures/expected-results.json).

level.description: Confidence level as a fraction, e.g. 0.8 for an 80% interval. Exclusive range (0, 1) -- 0 and 1 are both degenerate (sol architect-review 2nd round must B: 1.5 and other out-of-[0,1] values were already excluded by `minimum`, but that alone let 0 and 1 themselves and anything above 1 up to a boundary slip through; exclusiveMinimum/exclusiveMaximum close both ends).

calibration_sample_size.description: sol architect-review 3rd round must2: minimum 1, not 0 -- a leave-one-out calibration computed from zero samples is not a calibration, it's the absence of one (which is exactly what status=="insufficient_data" already represents).

coverage_history.description: frozen_predictions_only is always true in v2: a prediction, once recorded, is never retroactively rewritten when later evidence arrives -- only new revisions get appended (see docs/protocols/estimate-v2.md, mirroring trace/v1's append-only supersedes model).

digest_provenance_entry.description: One of three honest states for how a single cohort digest field's referenced object can be recovered -- see `cohort.cohort_provenance`'s own description for the full rationale. `kind` is the closed discriminator (this schema's own convention elsewhere, e.g. `decision.status`/`applicability.status`/`drift.status`, all closed enums rather than field-presence inference) that selects which of the three shapes below applies; the allOf/if/then block enforces that the field its `kind` requires is actually present, not merely conventionally expected.

object.description: REQUIRED when kind=="inline". The pre-normalization policy object itself (arbitrary shape -- this schema does not constrain what a routing/prompt/execution policy object looks like, only that recomputing sha256(JCS(object)) via contracts/shared/jcs.mjs must equal the sibling cohort digest field's value). This is the strongest of the three states: contracts/shared/verify-cohort-provenance.mjs recomputes and compares it, with no filesystem or network access, so this check runs unconditionally in CI.

uri.description: REQUIRED when kind=="locator". Where the referenced policy object can be found -- a path (optionally paired with `source_repo` when it is relative to a different repo than this one, mirroring decision/v1's $defs/artifact_ref convention) or any other stable locator a human or later tooling could use to go find the actual object. contracts/shared/verify-cohort-provenance.mjs does not attempt to fetch or hash whatever `uri` names (a JCS-normalized-object digest cannot be re-derived from raw file bytes the way an artifact_ref's byte-for-byte digest can) -- it only checks that `uri` is present and reports the entry as unverifiable, always, never silently treated as passing.

source_repo.description: Optional, only meaningful alongside `uri` under kind=="locator": set when `uri` is relative to a DIFFERENT repo than this one (same convention as decision/v1's $defs/artifact_ref `source_repo`). Never present under any other `kind`.

reason.description: REQUIRED when kind=="unavailable". Why no locator or inline object can be recorded (e.g. the policy object lives in a private repo that cannot be shared, or predates this field and was never persisted anywhere). This is the honest 'cannot be resolved' state -- it is never used to mean 'no referent is needed,' which this schema does not represent at all (all three digest fields are unconditionally required, so their provenance is always either resolvable or honestly marked unresolvable).

notes.description: Optional free-text annotation, e.g. marking a fixture's `object`/`uri` as synthetic rather than a real policy object. Never load-bearing for verification.

allOf.description: kind=="inline" requires `object` -- the whole point of this state is having the actual object on hand to recompute against.
kind=="locator" requires `uri` -- a locator that names nothing locates nothing.
kind=="unavailable" requires `reason` -- an unresolvable reference must say why, not just assert that it is unresolvable.
